tier_reason: The docs.rs page makes the xxHash/MetroHash claim ('around 3-20% improvement') with no xxHash numbers and no methodology, and the repo's benches/bench.rs (criterion) times only SeaHash. The well-known independent SMHasher suite (rurban, C port seahash.c) contradicts the xxHash, MetroHash and CityHash claims but does show a bulk-throughput win over FNV-1a/FNV-64 and MurmurHash3. So for the corrected baseline this is B: independent suite, CPU named but compiler and flags not stated, so not A.

corrections.baseline: FNV-1a / FNV-64 and MurmurHash3 (large-buffer bulk throughput); NOT xxHash, MetroHash or CityHash, which the independent SMHasher run shows are faster
corrections.workload: SMHasher bulk speed test (262144-byte keys, alignments 0-7, averaged) plus small-key test (1-31 byte keys, cycles/hash); the author's docs.rs figures give no dataset or size
corrections.claimed_speedup: Author (docs.rs 2.0.0 / README): 'around 3-20% improvement' over xxHash and MetroHash with no xxHash/MetroHash numbers shown; 5.9-6.7 GB/s on a '2.5 GHz CPU' vs CityHash ~1 GB/s, MurmurHash ~2.6 GB/s, FNV ~0.5 GB/s. Independent SMHasher (C port, bulk MiB/s): SeaHash 8240.58 vs FNV1a 754.70 / FNV64 747.70 (~11x, derived from page data) and Murmur3F 7104.08 (~1.16x, derived from page data), but SLOWER than xxHash64 11176.72 (~1.36x slower), metrohash64 14209.14, City64 14390.09 and xxh3 20853.74. Small keys: 58.61 cycles/hash vs FNV1a 75.28, Murmur3F 52.69, xxHash64 49.67.
corrections.hardware: SMHasher default table: AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz (label from SMHasher README); author's own figures: unspecified '2.5 GHz CPU'
corrections.stars_or_usage: 4 GitLab stars; crates.io 153,332,761 total downloads, 192 reverse dependencies (checked 2026-09-26)
corrections.caveats: The headline claim (3-20% faster than xxHash/MetroHash, faster than CityHash ~1 GB/s) is first-party, 2016-era, has no xxHash numbers, and is contradicted by independent SMHasher, where xxHash64, MetroHash64 and City64 all beat SeaHash in bulk throughput (and XXH3 is ~2.5x faster). SeaHash beats only FNV (~11x bulk) and MurmurHash3 (~16% bulk; it loses to Murmur3F on small keys). SMHasher tests a C port (seahash.c), not this Rust crate. The repo's benches/bench.rs (criterion) times SeaHash alone with no competitor, and no compiler/flags are stated anywhere. No commits since 2023-10-25.

notes: The claimed win over the listed baseline (xxHash) is refuted by SMHasher, so the entry survives only after re-baselining to FNV/MurmurHash3, which the docs.rs page also compares against. If the orchestrator wants only in-list baselines (xxHash, wyhash, CityHash, std::hash), treat this as reject not-faster.
